question: Does a per-task class-balanced LightGBM on a shared PCA representation beat a standard shared-hidden-layer MLP on every related classification task, not just on average, using scikit-learn's digits data?
method: Derive three binary tasks (is-even, is-greater-than-4, is-prime) from the digit label. One stratified 70/30 split. Compare a shared-hidden-layer MLP with per-task class-balanced LightGBM on standardised pixels plus PCA components. Hyper-parameters chosen by 5-fold CV on train only; test used once. Seeds 42, 43, 44.
metric_name: macro-F1 averaged over 3 binary tasks (is_even, is_gt_4, is_prime)
baseline: Standard hard-parameter-sharing MLP: one shared hidden layer, sigmoid multi-label outputs (sklearn MLPClassifier) on standardised pixels; hidden size and alpha chosen by train-only CV.
improved: Per-task class-balanced LightGBM on standardised pixels concatenated with 30 PCA components (fit on training pixels); num_leaves, learning_rate, n_estimators and colsample_bytree chosen per task by train-only 5-fold CV over a 24-configuration grid.
notes: Only one train/test split is used, so split-to-split variance is not measured; seeds capture model randomness only. The three tasks are deterministic functions of one label and therefore strongly related; the test set is small, so per-task gaps of a few points may be noise. Both models get the same 5-fold CV folds per seed; the baseline grid has 4 configurations and the LightGBM grid has 24 per task. The LightGBM model receives the same standardised pixels the baseline uses, plus PCA components. PCA dimension is fixed, not tuned. The paper's architecture is not specified in the provided abstract, so this is not a replication of its method. load_digits is bundled, so no network download or retry logic is needed.
